> 以下的详细说明为原文 —— 摘要与标题已翻译。

PCA is the SVD of the centred (by default also unit-variance) matrix Xc = U S V^T: scores U S, loadings V, eigenvalues S^2/(n-1) (the covariance or correlation eigenvalues — the tests check this identity).

The number of components is reported three ways, because each fails differently:

• cumulative — the smallest count reaching threshold of the variance (a convention, not a test: with many noisy columns it keeps noise);

• parallel — Horn's parallel analysis (Horn 1965): keep component i while its eigenvalue exceeds the parallel_stat ("mean" as in Horn, or "p95") of the i-th eigenvalue of n_parallel normal random tables of the same shape treated the same way;

• mdl — the MDL criterion of Wax & Kailath 1985 (mathspectral.n_sources_mdl, reused) on the centred data; it assumes white noise of equal variance in every column, which standardising breaks, so it is computed only with standardize=False (homogeneous columns: pixels, features in one unit) and is None otherwise.

n_components fixes how many scores/loadings to return (default: the parallel count, at least 1). Accepts a matrix or a feat_image_vector table.
